key_insight: DMAIC with two-level Fuzzy AHP identified defects as the dominant waste and ranked Machine, Method, and Man as the leading potential cause categories in robotic sidebeam bogie-frame welding.
engineering_relevance: The proposed improvement roadmap targets seam tracking, robot parameters, jig and fixture positioning, tack welding, and fit-up control to address welding quality and production inefficiency.
method: DMAIC with value stream mapping, time study, u′-control chart, DPMO, and sigma-level analysis.
Two-level Fuzzy AHP using judgments from ten experts to prioritize waste and potential cause categories.
6M fishbone analysis and corrective-action records to develop an improvement roadmap.
evidence_signal: Across 21 inspected units, 485 welding defects yielded 136,658.21 DPMO and a 2.60 sigma level; undercut represented 57.1% of defects, while process cycle efficiency was 4.88%.
watch_item: Weak expert agreement and sensitivity to respondent selection limit confidence in the rankings; proposed improvements still require implementation and empirical validation.
paper_title: Integration of DMAIC and Two-Level Fuzzy AHP for Diagnosing and Prioritizing Waste and Potential Causes of Welding Defects in a Sidebeam Bogie Frame
